==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|furnysshen}}, from {{der|en|fro||furniss-}}, stem of certain parts of {{m|fro|furnir}}, {{m|fro|fornir}} (Modern {{cog|fr|fournir}}), from {{der|en|gem}}, from {{der|en|frk|*frumjan||to complete, execute}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*frumjaną||to further, promote}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*promo-||front, forward}}. 

Cognate with {{cog|goh|frumjan||to perform, provide}}, {{cog|goh|fruma||utility, gain}}, {{cog|ang|fremu||profit, advantage}}, {{cog|ang|fremian||to promote, perform}}. More at {{m|en|frame}}, {{m|en|frim}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈfɝnɪʃ/|a=GA}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈfɜːnɪʃ/|a=RP}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-furnish.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɜː(ɹ)nɪʃ|s=2}}
* {{hyph|en|fur|nish}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}} <!-- Use Scholar to find cites for plural (many) "the-furnishes-were" -->

# [[material|Material]] used to [[create]] an [[engineered]] product.
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2003|author=Martin E. Rogers; Timothy E. Long|title=Synthetic Methods in Step-growth Polymers|publisher=Wiley|journal=IEEE|page=257
|passage=The resin-coated '''furnish''' is evenly spread inside the form and another metal plate is placed on top.}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To provide a [[place]] with [[furniture]], or other [[equipment]].
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|IV|58|The Celebrity, by arts unknown, induced Mrs. Judge Short and two other ladies to call at Mohair on a certain afternoon when Mr. Cooke was trying a trotter on the track. The three returned wondering and charmed with Mrs. Cooke; they were sure she had had no hand in the '''furnishing''' of that atrocious house.}}
#* {{RQ:Belloc Lowndes Lodger|II|17|Then his sallow face brightened, for the hall had been carefully '''furnished''', and was very clean. ¶ There was a neat hat-and-umbrella stand, and the stranger's weary feet fell soft on a good, serviceable dark-red drugget, which matched in colour the flock-paper on the walls.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|figuratively}} To [[supply]] or [[give]] (something).
#* {{RQ:Swift Free Thoughts|page=3|passage={{...}} Miniſters are ſo wiſe to leave their Proceedings to be accounted for by Reaſoners at a Diſtance, who often mould them into Syſtems, that do not only go down very well in the Coffee-Houſe, but are Supplies for Pamphlets in the preſent Age, and may probably '''furniſh''' Materials for Memoirs and Hiſtories in the next.}}
#* {{RQ:Austen Pride and Prejudice|volume=II|chapter=VI|page=67|passage=[H]e took his seat at the bottom of the table, by her ladyship's desire, and looked as if he felt that life could '''furnish''' nothing greater.}}
#* {{RQ:Macaulay History of England|volume=I|chapter=IV|page=507|passage=But his writings and his life '''furnish''' abundant proofs that he was not a man of strong sense.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|figuratively}} To [[supply]] (somebody) with something.
#: {{ux|en|The street outside my window '''furnish'''es meager entertainment.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|title=[An Accompt of Some Books.] III. ''Ottonis Tachenii Hippocrates Chymicus.'' Venetiis in 12º.|journal=[[w:Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society|Philosophical Transactions: Giving Some Accompt of the Present Undertakings, Studies and Labours of the Ingenious in Many Considerable Parts of the World]]|location=London|publisher=Printed by T. N. for John Martyn{{...|at the Bell, a little without Temple-Bar}}, printer to the {{w|Royal Society}}|date={{J2G|16 August 1669}}|year_published=1670|volume=IV|issue=50|pages=1019–1020|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=7sFeAAAAcAAJ&pg=PA1020|oclc=630046584|passage=For, that the ordure, which continually gathers on the skin, would ſoon ſtop the pores of it, if the ſweat were not '''furniſht''' with ſome efficacious diſſolvent to open and pierce them.}}
#* {{RQ:Swift Gulliver|part=II|page=247|passage=I was every day '''furniſhing''' the Court with ſome ridiculous Story; and ''Glumdalclitch'', although ſhe loved me to Exceſs, yet was arch enough to inform the Queen, whenever I committed any Folly that ſhe thought would be diverting to her Majeſty.}}
#* {{RQ:Le Fanu House|volume=I|page=304|passage={{...}} Mrs. Irons rebelled in her bed, and refused peremptorily to get up again, to '''furnish''' the musical topers with rum and lemons, {{...}}}}
